Erin —

Thanks for the package and quick turnaround. We received the three files and ran an initial read. A few high-level items from our side before we go line-by-line:

1) Liability cap: Redwood's standard for partner integrations is 3x monthly recurring revenue (MRR) or $250k, whichever is higher, for partner-developed integrations. We're open to discussing and can share a one-pager with rationale.

2) Subprocessor notice: We cannot accept unilateral subprocessor onboarding without at least a 10-business-day prior notice and an exception process for high-risk providers (e.g., hosting in new regions, new KMS providers).

3) DPA audit: Right-to-audit is acceptable — we prefer in-scope audits to be limited to SOC2 Type II reports and a mutually agreed on-site or third-party audit only for material security concerns. Thirty days' notice is tight; propose 45 days and cost-allocation for any intrusive audits.

4) Data transfer: The DPA must include explicit controls for cross-border transfers and indicate whether BrightArc will act as a subprocessor to Redwood's customers.

5) SOW: Milestone acceptance criteria need to map to Redwood's internal release checklist (I can attach). Also need better definition of support SLAs post-go-live.

Can Marcus / Laura weigh in on commercial and legal trade-offs? If we can converge on these 5 items, I'll propose a short call next week (30 min) to resolve the rest.

Thanks,

All —

Draft positions below that I can put into tracked changes if you want:

- Liability: Redwood accepts cap of (i) direct damages only; (ii) cap = the greater of $300,000 or six months' average monthly fees paid under this Agreement, but carve out for gross negligence and willful misconduct and IP indemnity.
- Subprocessors: BrightArc must provide a list of subprocessors and 10 business days' prior written notice. For high-risk subprocessors (processing customer PII or encryption key management), written consent required; otherwise a right to object within that 10-day window.
- Audit: Accept SOC 2 Type II reports annually for routine compliance. Right to third-party on-site audit only when material breach suspected; any on-site audit costs shall be borne by the requesting party unless breach is substantiated. 45 days' notice for non-urgent audits.
- Data transfer: Require SCCs for EU transfers, and where BrightArc acts as a subprocessor to Redwood's customers it must execute a direct DPA with the customer or agree to Redwood's flow-down terms.
- SOW SLAs: 4-hour P1 response, 24-hour P2, acceptance testing to include functional tests, performance tests, and security checklist. Payment tied to milestone acceptance with 15% withheld until 30 days post-go-live to cover defects.

If you approve these positions I will generate tracked-change redlines and a negotiation memo for the call.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
